title: cni-ebpf-dataplane-corruption-dns-blackout-notes
content:
Incident summary:

On 2025-11-02 03:12 UTC we observed a cluster-wide DNS blackbox: service/resolution failures for many system and app pods across multiple nodes in us-west-2. Symptoms included: pod-level DNS timeouts (CoreDNS), TCP connection resets to kube-apiserver from some nodes, and erratic pod readiness transitions. Impact: ~30% of application traffic failed short requests; intermittent control-plane slowness for cluster admin operations.

Initial detection:
- Pager on-call alerted by external SLO alerts (5xx ramp) at 03:12 UTC.
- SRE runbook checks flagged elevated pod restart rate and CoreDNS failures at 03:16.
- Grafana: spike in DNS query latency (core-dns) and conntrack table growth on certain nodes.

Key hypothesis formed in first 30 minutes: CNI dataplane (eBPF program) corrupted, causing packet forwarding blackholes and causing DNS/timeouts; conntrack entries leaked leading to ephemeral port exhaustion on nodes.

Timeline (UTC):
- 03:12 Alert: external 5xx SLO triggered (increased from 0.2% to 8%)
- 03:15 Oncall (Evan) checks: core-dns pods showing SERVFAIL in logs, high kubedns latency metric.
- 03:18 Observed node-level metrics: conntrack_count per-node trending up on nodes ip-*-u10-*.
- 03:22 SSH to affected node (ip-10-5-4-23): netstat shows very large number of TIME-WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT sockets; ipvs rules appear intact.
- 03:25 bpftool list shows eBPF program mismatches on affected nodes (program id differs from expected). bpftool prog show output excerpt: "prog type xdp id 4129 tag 2f3c... (expected id 3921)"
- 03:30 Observed kube-proxy logs with repeated conntrack: "failed to ensure conntrack rule - conntrack table full" on node 10.5.4.23
- 03:36 Applied temporary mitigation: rolled out CNI dataplane restart (systemd restart cni-agent) on 3 most affected nodes; partial improvement in DNS latencies on those nodes within 90s.
- 04:15 Scaled CoreDNS horizontally (added two replicas) as precaution for query backpressure.
- 04:40 Full cluster sweep to restart cni-agent on remaining flagged nodes.
- 06:00 Alert volume reduced and SLOs back to nominal; incident declared mitigated.

Impact breakdown:
- Affected components: pod networking (cluster overlay), DNS (CoreDNS), kube-proxy/conntrack behavior.
- Customer-visible: intermittent request failures and elevated latencies for API surfaces relying on in-cluster DNS (webhooks, service discovery).
- Control-plane: kubectl exec/port-forward sometimes timed out during the peak.

Root cause hypothesis (working):
- The CNI plugin uses an eBPF-based dataplane for packet steering. An out-of-band code path in the plugin (hot-reload) attempted to update eBPF maps/programs while dataplane traffic was still in-flight. On ~10 nodes a race caused an invalid program to be attached (or map keys corrupted) producing forward blackholes for DNAT/masquerade paths and preventing conntrack entries from being maintained properly. As conntrack entries failed to be swept or garbage-collected correctly, conntrack table sizes ballooned and the kernel started rejecting new entries, causing connection failures.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- bpftool outputs with mismatched program tags between node agent and desired artifact (artifact tag: 9f8b, live tag: 2f3c).
- dmesg lines on affected hosts referencing "bpf: invalid insn" and then subsequent "bpf: program failed attach" around 03:14-03:20.
- kernel conntrack logs: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" in syslog on affected nodes.
- Rolling restart of cni-agent returned nodes to healthy state quickly.

Mitigations performed during incident (chronological):
1) Scoped restarts of cni-agent on highest-conntrack nodes to restore correct eBPF programs (03:36 onward).
2) Added temporary IPTABLES fallback for masquerade on nodes where dataplane restart failed (manual iptables nat POSTROUTING ACCEPT rule to allow traffic to egress).
3) Scaled CoreDNS to absorb retry load while network flakiness resolved (04:15).
4) Throttled autopatcher that had been pushing hot-reload of the CNI component (rolled back last hotfix at 04:50).

Short-term follow-ups assigned (owners):
- Aisha: add automatic bpftool checksum comparison in node healthcheck; fail node as NotReady if checksum mismatch (JIRA-OPS-1628).
- Connor: implement conntrack gauge alert in Prometheus with lower threshold and alerting action (reduce false negatives).
- Marta: add an emergency runbook section for "ebpf dataplane corruption" with commands to collect bpftool, dmesg, and conntrack exports.

Draft runbook additions (for SRE-runbooks -> networking):
- Detection checks (fast):
  - kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady
  - kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=coredns -o wide; check restarts
  - for node in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do ssh $node sudo bpftool prog show | grep -q "EXPECTED_TAG" || echo $node; done  # (replace EXPECTED_TAG)
- Immediate mitigation steps:
  1) On affected node(s): sudo systemctl restart cni-agent.service (watch bpftool prog show to confirm expected tag)
  2) If restart fails repeatedly: apply iptables NAT accept shim: sudo iptables -t nat -I POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j ACCEPT (document interface naming)
  3) If conntrack table near capacity: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l; if > 80% of nf_conntrack_max, run sudo conntrack -F on degraded node after confirming blast radius (coordinate with app teams)
- Data collection commands (one-liners to paste into incident channel):
  - bpftool prog show --json | jq '.[] | {id,tag,attach_type}' | head -n 50
  - sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 200 | grep conntrack
  - sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max; sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
  - sudo iptables -t nat -S | sed -n '1,200p'

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did hot-reload path attempt attach on nodes with different kernel/bpf ABI? Are we missing a node affinity filter in the rollout?
- Was there a correlated kernel update churn in the same timeframe? (preliminary check: no kernel upgrades were scheduled but need to confirm images rotated by autoscaler).
- Is conntrack max tuned appropriately for our high-pps services? Need SRE + platform to model the worst-case expected ephemeral ports.

Post-incident actions (30/60/90 days):
- 7d (owner: Connor): add Prometheus node exporter metric compare for bpftool tag and set an alert -> create automation to cordon+drain if mismatch persists for 5 minutes.
- 14d (owner: Marta): publish final runbook entry for eBPF dataplane failure with playbook commands and escalation matrix.
- 30d (owner: Aisha): harden CNI hot-reload: perform server-side validation of target node kernel features and do canary only on nodes with matching bpftool tags; introduce safer attach sequence (quiesce traffic, swap maps atomically).
- 60d (owner: Platform): review nf_conntrack_max sizing and autoscaling to ensure safe headroom; consider per-node conntrack partitioning or increased table size.
- 90d: run chaos experiment in staging that simulates an eBPF program reload failure and validate runbook + automation.

Notes to on-call and SREs (informal):
- If you see "invalid insn" messages in dmesg after an upgrade/hot-reload, don't immediately reboot nodes. Try cni-agent restart and bpftool inspect. Reboot as last resort because that can disrupt more state.
- Keep a spare control-plane capacity when doing cluster-wide dataplane rollouts. We were lucky CoreDNS scaling buffered things.

Appendix (raw snippets):
- bpftool diff (edge): 
  EXPECTED_TAG=9f8b
  sudo bpftool prog show | grep -E "id|tag" | sed -n '1,120p'
  // sample live output showing tag 2f3c (mismatch)

- syslog excerpt: 
  Nov 02 03:18 ip-10-5-4-23 kernel: [18345.123456] bpf: invalid insn 0x20 at 174
  Nov 02 03:19 ip-10-5-4-23 kernel: [18346.987654] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet

- Example Slack snippet that helped coordinate node restarts:
  "evan: restarting cni-agent on 10.5.4.23 -> bpftool now shows tag 9f8b; DNS rtt for pods back to 12ms"

Draft severity & blameless notes:
- Severity: Sev2 (customer impact moderate, mitigation within 3 hours)
- Blameless: this looks like insufficient safety checks during a hot-reload path; we should avoid finger-pointing and focus on automation/test coverage.

Immediate TODO (before postmortem):
- Collect full bpftool/prog dumps from all nodes (Aisha)
- Create a canary gating job to validate bpftool tag signatures prior to rolling reloads (Aisha, due 2025-11-09)
- Draft the final postmortem (this doc -> postmortem) with attachments and timeline extracted from alerts and logs (Evan, due 2025-11-06)

If anything missing or you want raw logs, ping me in #sre-incident with the ticket JIRA-OPS-1628.

-- Evan
